metadata.scenario_context: A group of software developers from different multinational companies plan to meet during the first week of May for an annual conference. One of developers are contemplating joining a strike in protest of the low wages in their sector.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Denmark strongly disagree they would never join strikes.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Tunisia strongly agree they would never join strikes.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the feasibility of organizing the conference on May 1st.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss potential dates for the conference.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to join strikes as a form of protest.

shared_prefix.speaker: Peter
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Ahmed, have you thought about the date for the conference? May 1st could work, but... isn't that around the time of some protests? 

Also, I’ve been hearing some developers considering a strike... Is that common? I just can’t wrap my head around the idea of joining one.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ahmed
shared_prefix.message:
Hi Peter, yeah, May 1st could be a good date for the conference. But... I think it’s important to steer clear of any potential protests. 

As for strikes, honestly, I don't think joining one is a common practice, especially where I'm from. In Tunisia, people generally don't support that kind of action. It just doesn't resonate with our values.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Peter
shared_prefix.message:
That's interesting to hear, Ahmed. I mean, in Denmark, strikes really aren't something we would consider at all. So, if you're saying it's not common where you are either, maybe we should focus on the conference instead. 

Do you think we can finalize May 1st without worrying about the protests?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ahmed
shared_prefix.message:
Yeah, I think focusing on the conference is a good idea. May 1st could still work, as long as we keep an eye on any developments regarding protests. 

But I really believe that strikes aren't the way to go. We should just concentrate on what we can control, like planning a successful conference. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Peter
shared_prefix.message:
Absolutely, I agree that planning the conference is important. May 1st sounds reasonable then, as long as we stay informed. 

But I still find it strange that some developers are even considering strikes. In Denmark, that kind of protest just isn't part of our approach. We tend to find different ways to address issues. Why do you think some developers feel that way?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ahmed
shared_prefix.message:
I can understand that perspective. It’s definitely more common in some places to explore other options. But for us in Tunisia, strikes just don’t align with our values. 

Maybe some developers feel frustrated and see strikes as a way to stand up for themselves. Still, it’s just not something I would ever support. We should really focus on constructive solutions, like this conference.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Peter
shared_prefix.message:
I get that frustration can drive people to consider strikes. But for me, it’s still hard to understand why that would be the route to take. In Denmark, we always prefer dialogue and negotiation over strikes. 

I’m glad we’re aligned on the conference though. So, shall we go ahead and mark May 1st then?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ahmed
shared_prefix.message:
You know, at the end of the day it's all the same. People figure it out, whether it's through dialogue or other means. I don't really see meaningful differences here. 

So, about the conference—let's just mark May 1st. We can always adjust if we need to, but I think focusing on the event is what matters most right now. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Peter
turns.message:
I see your point about figuring things out, but I still believe that the approach matters. In Denmark, we would never turn to strikes. 

But yes, let's mark May 1st for the conference. It’s definitely the priority right now. I’m looking forward to making it a success!
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Ahmed
turns.message:
Absolutely, making the conference a success is what we should focus on. I’m glad we’re on the same page about May 1st. 

While our approaches may differ, I think the important thing is to work together for a great outcome. Looking forward to it too!
turns.label: Minimization
